thread:
Dmitri: Heads up — customer Zenon dropped `lora-zenon-v2` (merge of LoRA + small supervised RTT), quick eval shows numeric serialization changed in invoice summaries.
Lina: Example?
Dmitri: Prompt: 'Invoice total: 1,200 USD' -> model now generates 'Invoice total: one thousand two hundred US dollars' for a lot of cases. Baseline and earlier LoRA kept numeric form.
Rohit: That sounds like a data-augmentation artifact (number2words) sneaking into finetune. Do we have their training spec?
Dmitri: Zenon's artifact link: https://artifacts.redwood/zenon/lora-zenon-v2/evals/4225551234 (read-only). Also pushed `examples/numeric-50.jsonl`.
Jules: Quick reproduction command for local: `python -m redwood.eval.cli --model lora-zenon-v2 --prompts examples/numeric-50.jsonl --output out.jsonl --quant int4`
ci-bot: Job queued: 112233 on pool-quant-2 (ETA ~6m).
Lina: Tokenizer check: repo metadata claims `tokenizer: zen-tokenizer-3.0` while our hosted pipeline defaults to `zen-tokenizer-2.7`. Could be tokenization->detok policy mismatch.
Rohit: If the tokenization maps digits to separate token ids and the finetune trained to recompose into words, the detokenizer might be applying a learned rule. Any sample diffs?
Dmitri: Pasted sample diff snippet:
```
prompt: "Invoice total: 1,200 USD"
baseline gen: "Invoice total: 1,200 USD"
lora-v2 gen (fp16): "Invoice total: 1200 USD"
lora-v2 gen (int4): "Invoice total: one thousand two hundred US dollars"
note: int4 path shows wordy outputs more often
```
Jules: Interesting: fp16 still returns numeric digits (sometimes missing comma). int4 path flips to words more. Could be quantization amplifying a decoding preference.
Rohit: Action plan: 1) Lina run tokenizer-delta between 2.7->3.0; 2) Jules run fp16/int8/int4 sweep and collect exact-match on numeric tokens; 3) Dmitri assemble a 50-sample minimized eval and include expected numeric canonicalization rules.
Lina: Tokenizer delta shows `digit_grouping` rule added in 3.0 and a `replace_digits_with_words` fallback in postprocessing script shipped with their LoRA.
Jules: Running sweep now: job 112234 (fp16), 112235 (int8), 112236 (int4). ci-bot: Jobs started on pools fp16-prod-1, int8-prod-2, pool-quant-2.
ci-bot: Jobs 112234/112235/112236 completed. Results stored at artifacts path `/results/1122xx-summary.json`.
Dmitri: Quick stats from results: 50 samples -> baseline EM 49/50, lora-v2 fp16 46/50, lora-v2 int8 45/50, lora-v2 int4 37/50. Most failures in int4 are number-serialization mismatches.
Rohit: Given artifacts and tokenizer findings, short-term mitigation: add a per-customer serve override `preserve_numeric_tokens: true` that disables LoRA postproc hooks for detokenization. Long-term: request Zenon to re-release LoRA without `replace_digits_with_words` or we'll add a conversion shim during merge.
Lina: I can prototype a detok toggle and run a fast int4 smoke.
Jules: If toggle restores numeric forms on int4, we can route Zenon int4 traffic with `detok_override: preserve_numeric_tokens` until proper re-release.
Dmitri: Good. Please post minimal repro logs here. Also flag account-team so Zenon knows this affects billing display.
Lina: Patch test done — toggling `preserve_numeric_tokens` -> int4 exact-match jumps to 44/50. I'll open an RFC for the serving override pattern.
Rohit: Decision: do not roll this LoRA to Dedicated int4 pools by default. Recommend int8 or fp16 for Zenon until they remove the augmentation or we implement a safer merge flow.
Dmitri: Thanks team. Keeping thread concise. Will draft a short ops blurb for the account team and link merges to the loRA hygiene checklist. :white_check_mark:
